subject: Re: Proposed compromise language for IP indemnity / liability-cap carve-out
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Legal Ops <legalops@acme-corp.com>, Tom Vega <tom.vega@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed compromise language for IP indemnity / liability-cap carve-out

Team / Tom —

Following our call this week, I pulled together a narrow compromise that keeps a liability cap but preserves Acme’s ability to recover for third-party IP claims that we indemnify. The core asks from Acme were: (1) carve IP indemnity out of the monetary cap entirely, and (2) a low evidence threshold for triggering indemnity. We think both are broad as drafted, so the goal here is to propose precise, negotiable language that limits exposure while addressing Acme’s concern.

High-level proposal (attached as redline):
- Keep the overall monetary cap in the MSA (monthly/annual cap remains for non-IP claims).
- Carve out third-party IP infringement claims that Redwood is obligated to indemnify, but limit the carve-out to: (i) amounts equal to final judgments and settlements actually paid arising from such claims, and (ii) reasonable, documented defense and settlement costs (counsel fees, court costs).
- Require claimant notice + our right to assume defense (standard control of defense clause). Failure to timely notify that prevents defense/control forfeits the carve-out for that claim.
- Add an evidence/checklist requirement: Acme must provide (a) claim notice, (b) copy of the claim/assertion, (c) evidence of alleged infringement (e.g., claim letters, allegedly infringing materials), and (d) reasonable cooperation. This prevents speculative or unsupported notices from creating open-ended exposure.

Proposed redline snippet (for the MSA liability section):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the aggregate liability cap set forth in Section [X] shall not apply to amounts that Redwood is required to pay under Section [Y] (Indemnification for Intellectual Property Infringement) arising from third-party claims, provided that: (a) Customer provides notice of the claim, a copy of the claim or complaint, and any available supporting documentation reasonably necessary for Redwood to evaluate the claim; (b) Customer allows Redwood sole control of the defense and settlement (subject to Customer’s reasonable consent for settlements that require monetary payment by Customer); and (c) amounts recoverable under this carve-out are limited to (i) final judgments and settlements actually paid, and (ii) documented, reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs incurred in the defense and settlement of the claim.  Failure by Customer to provide the notice and documentation specified in (a) in a timely fashion that materially prejudices Redwood’s ability to defend shall relieve Redwood of liability under this carve-out for the affected claim."

Questions for internal review:
- Do we want to include a sunset / aggregation rule (e.g., multiple claims in a 12-month period treated as one)?
- Is the "final judgments and settlements actually paid" language acceptable or should we broaden to include "amounts finally agreed"?
- Should we require customer to help produce evidence (samples of alleged infringing content) within X days?

I’ve attached a redline and a short evidence-checklist draft. Please comment — Marissa and Laura, any legal flags before I send to Tom?

Thanks,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for circulating. Appreciate the effort to narrow this. A few quick points from our side:

1) Carve-out scope: we need the carve-out to cover "infringement of Customer content and Customer’s authorized use" of the service — not only claims that assert Redwood product code. Can that be reflected?

2) Evidence burden: Acme cannot realistically produce full technical analysis at notice. We need a modest threshold that allows early preservation of rights (e.g., claimant letter + basic sample). We’re fine with producing further materials on request, but the initial trigger needs to be workable for a customer who lacks deep legal/technical teams.

3) Insurance/escrow: procurement prefers Redwood to carry an endorsements/insurance in support of this exposure (or at least a mechanism to aggregate payments). Can you confirm current insurance stack?

4) Control of defense: we accept you leading defense but request prior written notice before settling any claim that would impose monetary obligations on Acme.

If you want, we can hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to move to a resolution.

Tom
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed compromise language for IP indemnity / liability-cap carve-out

Ben —

Good capture. A few internal negotiation points:
- Scope tweak: we should accept covering "Customer content and Customer’s authorized use" but add a carve-out that excludes: (i) claims arising from Customer modifications, mashups, or embedding third-party models outside the Service’s documented connectors; (ii) Customer’s failure to comply with API Terms.
- Evidence threshold: propose a two-step approach: (1) initial notice + claimant letter + representative sample/materials (to trigger obligations), and (2) 30 days from notice for Customer to provide reasonable additional artifacts. If Customer cannot produce needed materials, the carve-out drops. That balances Acme’s operational constraints with our need to avoid speculative claims.
- Insurance: we should confirm current policy limits (I think $5M umbrella w/ tech E&O). If Acme wants higher, offer to discuss capped escrow or reinsurance language but do not accept unlimited liability.
- Aggregation: recommend treating related claims arising from the same product/version within 12 months as one occurrence for purposes of the cap/carve-out. Prevents multiplication.

If Ben will push this to Tom, highlight we need their help to gather initial materials but keep the timeline reasonable.

—Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Policy
Redwood Inference

Tom —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Below I incorporated both your ask re: Customer content and our internal guardrails. Two items to flag: our legal team will need at least a modest sample and the complaint/claim letter to assess potential exposure; it does not need to be a full technical report up front. Also, on insurance: Redwood carries a primary tech E&O policy with $2M each claim / $5M aggregate and a $5M umbrella; we’re happy to share certs and explore a limited escrow if Acme’s procurement requires additional comfort.

Refined redline (replace earlier snippet):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the monetary limitation of liability set forth in Section [X] shall not apply to amounts that Redwood is required to pay under Section [Y] (Indemnification for Intellectual Property Infringement) arising from third-party claims asserting infringement of Customer content or Customer’s authorized use of the Service, provided that: (a) Customer promptly provides written notice of the claim, a copy of the claim or complaint and any available supporting documentation (including any claimant correspondence and a representative sample of the allegedly infringing content or materials); (b) Customer cooperates with Redwood and uses commercially reasonable efforts to provide additional relevant materials within thirty (30) days of notice; (c) Customer’s right to indemnification is subject to Redwood’s right to assume and control the defense and settlement of such claim, provided that Redwood shall not settle any claim that requires Customer to pay money or admit fault without Customer’s prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld); and (d) amounts recoverable under this carve-out are limited to (i) final judgments and settlements actually paid by Redwood, and (ii) documented, reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs incurred in the defense and settlement of the claim.  The carve-out shall not apply to Claims to the extent they arise from (i) modifications to the Service made by Customer, (ii) Customer’s combination of the Service with third-party products or data in a manner not authorized by Redwood, or (iii) Customer’s breach of the API Terms or other misuse of the Service.  Related claims that arise from the same allegedly infringing product or version within a twelve (12) month period shall be aggregated as a single claim for purposes of this carve-out.  Failure by Customer to provide required notice and reasonable supporting documentation in a timely manner that materially prejudices Redwood’s ability to defend shall relieve Redwood of liability under this carve-out for the affected claim."

Next steps: I can send this redline formally (attached) and propose a 20-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT to finalize. Tom — does that work for you?

Ben
